places.name: Koch Family Children's Museum of Evansville (cMoe)
places.description: Hands-on children's museum downtown. Best with kids along.

places.name: Pigeon Creek Greenway
places.description: Paved multi-use path along Pigeon Creek and the Ohio River. Walk, run or bike.

places.name: Evansville Riverfront & Dress Plaza
places.description: Riverside walkway with views of the Ohio River, benches and sunsets.

places.name: Reitz Home Museum

places.name: Evansville Museum of Arts, History & Science

places.name: Haynie's Corner Arts District
places.description: Walkable arts district with galleries, murals, bars and restaurants. First Fridays in season.

places.name: Willard Library

places.name: USS LST-325 Ship Memorial

places.name: Evansville African American Museum

places.name: Garvin Park

places.name: Evansville Otters at Bosse Field

places.name: Mesker Park Zoo & Botanic Garden

places.name: Howell Wetlands

places.name: Wesselman Woods Nature Preserve

places.name: Eagle Slough Natural Area

places.name: Evansville Wartime Museum
places.description: WWII aircraft, vehicles and the story of Evansville's wartime factories.

places.name: Burdette Park
places.description: County park with trails, fishing lakes, and a summer aquatic center.

places.name: John James Audubon State Park

places.name: Angel Mounds State Historic Site

places.name: Newburgh Riverwalk & Historic District
places.description: Riverwalk, historic downtown, shops and restaurants.

places.name: Blue Grass Fish & Wildlife Area
places.description: Lakes and trails for fishing, kayaking and quiet walks.

places.name: Harmonie State Park
places.description: Wooded trails, Wabash River views, camping and a summer pool.

places.name: Historic New Harmony
places.description: Utopian-community town with walking tours, the Labyrinth, Roofless Church, shops and cafes.

places.name: Owensboro Museum of Fine Art
places.description: Regional art museum with stained glass and changing exhibits.

places.name: Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame & Museum
places.description: Interactive history of bluegrass music, plus concerts.

places.name: Owensboro Museum of Science & History
places.description: Local history, science exhibits and a NASCAR-themed gallery.

places.name: Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial

places.name: Patoka River National Wildlife Refuge

places.name: Holiday World & Splashin' Safari
places.description: Theme park with wooden coasters and a water park.

places.name: George Rogers Clark National Historical Park
places.description: Revolutionary War memorial on the Wabash River.

places.name: Red Skelton Museum of American Comedy
places.description: Exhibits on Red Skelton and the history of American comedy.

places.name: Garden of the Gods (Shawnee National Forest)
places.description: Sandstone formations with a short scenic loop and longer trails.

places.name: Hoosier National Forest (Tell City district)
places.description: Forest trails, overlooks and lakes like German Ridge and Celina Lake.

places.name: Patoka Lake
places.description: Large lake with beach, boating, trails and camping.

places.name: Cedarhurst Center for the Arts
places.description: Art museum and outdoor sculpture park on wooded grounds.

places.name: Janice Mason Art Museum
places.description: Small-town art museum near Lake Barkley.

places.name: Corydon Capitol State Historic Site
places.description: Indiana's first state capitol and historic downtown.

places.name: River Discovery Center
places.description: River history museum with a towboat simulator.

places.name: Yeiser Art Center
places.description: Contemporary art center in downtown Paducah.

places.name: Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area
places.description: Huge recreation area: Elk & Bison Prairie, The Homeplace 1850s farm, planetarium, trails, lakes.

places.name: The Science Center
places.description: Hands-on science center.

places.name: National Corvette Museum
places.description: Corvette history, the famous sinkhole exhibit, and factory nearby.

places.name: Mammoth Cave National Park
places.description: World's longest known cave system. Ranger-led cave tours and surface trails.

places.name: Monroe County History Center
places.description: Local history museum.

places.name: WonderLab Museum
places.description: Hands-on science museum.

places.name: Speed Art Museum
places.description: Kentucky's largest art museum.

places.name: Kentucky Science Center
places.description: Your home science center. Three floors of hands-on exhibits plus a theater.

places.name: Frazier History Museum
places.description: History museum and the official start of the Kentucky Bourbon Trail.

places.name: The Filson Historical Society
places.description: Historic mansion and Kentucky history exhibits.

places.name: Customs House Museum & Cultural Center
places.description: Art and history museum with a model train layout.

places.name: Louisville Zoo
places.description: Large zoo with Glacier Run and Gorilla Forest.

places.name: Terre Haute Children's Museum
places.description: Hands-on science and children's museum.

places.name: Swope Art Museum
places.description: American art collection in an Art Deco building.

places.name: Fort Donelson National Battlefield
places.description: Civil War battlefield with a driving tour and river overlooks.

places.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park
places.description: Memorial building over Lincoln's symbolic birth cabin, plus his boyhood home site.

places.name: Historic Locust Grove
places.description: 18th-century farm site with house tours and grounds.

places.name: Frist Art Museum
places.description: Changing exhibitions in an Art Deco post office.

places.name: Adventure Science Center
places.description: Big hands-on science center with a planetarium.

places.name: Discovery Park of America
places.description: Huge museum and heritage park: science, history, nature.

places.name: Nashville Zoo
places.description: Zoo on a historic farm with lots of shade.

places.name: Indiana State Museum
places.description: State history, science and culture museum on the canal.

places.name: Indiana Historical Society
places.description: Interactive Indiana history experiences.

places.name: Kurt Vonnegut Museum & Library
places.description: Small museum on Kurt Vonnegut's life and work.

places.name: Newfields (Indianapolis Museum of Art)
places.description: Art museum with gardens and the Winterlights holiday show.

places.name: Gateway Arch National Park
places.description: Free museum under the Arch; tram ride to the top is ticketed.

places.name: World Chess Hall of Fame
places.description: Chess art and history exhibits. Giant chess piece out front.

places.name: Saint Louis Science Center
places.description: Free science center with a planetarium.

places.name: Saint Louis Zoo
places.description: Free world-class zoo in Forest Park.

places.name: Saint Louis Art Museum
places.description: Free art museum in Forest Park.

places.name: Laumeier Sculpture Park
places.description: Outdoor sculpture park with walking trails.

places.name: The Magic House
places.description: St. Louis Children's Museum.

places.name: Discovery Center at Murfree Spring
places.description: Children's science museum with wetlands outside.

places.name: University of Kentucky Art Museum
places.description: University art museum.

places.name: Living Arts & Science Center
places.description: Art and science center with a planetarium.

places.name: Cincinnati Museum Center
places.description: Union Terminal: natural history, history and children's museums.

places.name: Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden
places.description: One of the oldest US zoos. Festival of Lights in winter.

places.name: Memphis Zoo
places.description: Large zoo with Teton Trek, a Northwest Passage exhibit and an aquarium area.

places.name: Museum of Science & History (Pink Palace)
places.description: Science and history museum in the Pink Palace mansion.

places.name: Children's Museum of Memphis
places.description: Hands-on children's museum.

places.name: National Civil Rights Museum
places.description: At the Lorraine Motel where Dr. King was killed.

places.name: Willard Library and its Grey Lady ghost
places.description: Victorian library from the 1880s that is said to be haunted by a Grey Lady. It leans into the legend with ghost cams and October tours.

places.name: Grave of the Gypsy Queen
places.description: Oak Hill Cemetery holds the grave of Elizabeth Harrison, remembered as a queen of a traveling Romani family, buried here in 1900 after a huge funeral.

places.name: Giant Santa
places.description: A towering fiberglass Santa that has waved at Evansville drivers for decades. Quick photo stop.

places.name: Bosse Field, the League of Their Own ballpark
places.description: The third-oldest ballpark still in regular use in the country, and the home field of the Racine Belles in the 1992 movie.

places.name: Martini-drinking pink elephant
places.description: A big pink elephant in glasses holding a martini outside a liquor store just off US 41. One of the classic silly photo stops near home.

places.name: Weather rock and animal statues
places.description: A joke weather station (if the rock is wet, it's raining) surrounded by a herd of fiberglass animals.

places.name: Kitchen canister grain bins
places.description: Farm grain bins painted to look like a giant set of flour, sugar and coffee canisters.

places.name: Footprints of the Archangel Gabriel
places.description: A stone slab with two footprints that the Harmonist leader said were left by the angel Gabriel in the early 1800s.

places.name: The Roofless Church
places.description: A walled, open-air church by architect Philip Johnson with a shingled dome shaped like an upside-down rosebud. Calm and beautiful.

places.name: Harmonist Labyrinth
places.description: A hedge maze rebuilt from the Harmonists' original, with a little stone temple at the center.

places.name: Eight-legged calf
places.description: A preserved eight-legged calf kept among the curiosities in the town's old Working Men's Institute museum and library.

places.name: America's first Santa statue
places.description: A 22-foot concrete Santa from 1935 standing on a hill, dedicated to the children of the world.

places.name: Santa's Candy Castle
places.description: A 1930s brick castle candy shop famous for frozen hot chocolate and a huge wall of sweets.

places.name: Santa Claus Museum and the town post office letters
places.description: A small museum about the town that answers thousands of letters to Santa every year. You can write one yourself.

places.name: Dr. Ted's Musical Marvels
places.description: A collection of restored mechanical music machines: street organs, a giant dance organ and nickelodeons, all played on the tour.

places.name: Bronzed foundation of Lincoln's cabin
places.description: The hearth and sill logs of the Lincoln family cabin, recast in bronze on the spot where Abe grew up.

places.name: Lincoln Landing
places.description: The Ohio River bluff where a young Lincoln set off on a flatboat to New Orleans in 1828.

places.name: Shoe tree
places.description: A roadside tree hung with hundreds of pairs of old shoes. Bring a pair to add.

places.name: World's largest Celtic cross carved from one rock
places.description: A huge Celtic cross cut from a single block of sandstone, tucked in the Perry County hills.

places.name: Geode Grotto
places.description: A priest's handmade garden of shrines and walls covered in thousands of Indiana geodes.

places.name: Giant popcorn box
places.description: An oversized box of popcorn that makes a quick, goofy photo.

places.name: League Stadium, the Rockford Peaches ballpark
places.description: The wooden ballpark dressed up as the Peaches' home field for A League of Their Own. Still used for summer baseball.

places.name: Red Skelton Museum of American Comedy
places.description: Costumes, clown paintings and hands-on comedy exhibits for the Vincennes-born comedian.

places.name: Big pencil
places.description: A giant pencil standing on its point. Quick photo stop.

places.name: Big watermelon slice
places.description: A giant slice of watermelon celebrating Knox County's melon farms.

places.name: Indiana Military Museum
places.description: Tanks, aircraft and uniforms from the Civil War to today, with a big outdoor vehicle yard.

places.name: The Big Peach
places.description: A 20-foot peach on top of a tower beside a farm market on US 41.

places.name: Otis the fishing Sasquatch
places.description: A big wooden Bigfoot with a fishing pole.

places.name: Hagenbeck-Wallace circus diorama
places.description: A huge hand-carved miniature circus in the French Lick West Baden Museum, with thousands of tiny figures.

places.name: West Baden Springs dome
places.description: A 1902 hotel atrium under a 200-foot free-spanning dome, once called the eighth wonder of the world. Free to walk in and gawk.

places.name: Jug Rock
places.description: A 60-foot sandstone pillar shaped like a jug with a flat cap, hidden in the woods just off US 50.

places.name: Gus Grissom rocket monument
places.description: A 44-foot limestone rocket honoring the hometown astronaut.

places.name: Joe Palooka statue
places.description: A 10-foot limestone statue of the 1940s comic-strip boxer outside the town hall.

places.name: Foote's Tomb
places.description: A tomb carved straight into a limestone boulder in the 1840s by a local doctor.

places.name: Big brain with smart lighting
places.description: A giant anatomical brain sculpture on the IU campus that lights up at night.

places.name: Marengo Cave
places.description: A show cave found by two kids in 1883, with easy walking tours past big formations.

places.name: Constitution Elm stump
places.description: The preserved trunk of the tree that shaded the delegates who wrote Indiana's first constitution in 1816.

places.name: Colgate Clock
places.description: One of the largest clocks in the world, 40 feet across, facing Louisville from the old Colgate plant.

places.name: Stiffy Green the bulldog
places.description: A stuffed (really a statue) bulldog with glowing green eyes that local legend says guarded his master's tomb. Now in the county history museum.

places.name: Birthplace of the Coke bottle mural
places.description: A mural marking the city where the curvy Coca-Cola bottle was designed in 1915.

places.name: Monopoly board tombstone
places.description: A grave marker carved as a Monopoly board.

places.name: World's largest toilet
places.description: A giant toilet you can slide through at the kidscommons children's museum.

places.name: Graves of America's first train robbers
places.description: The Reno Gang pulled the first peacetime train robbery in 1866. Three brothers are buried together in the old city cemetery.

places.name: Founder of Mother's Day marker
places.description: Henderson teacher Mary Towles Sasseen held Mother's Day celebrations in the 1880s, years before it became a national holiday.

places.name: World's largest sassafras tree
places.description: A sassafras over 100 feet tall and several hundred years old, saved from a road-widening crew by a woman with a shotgun.

places.name: Burgoo pot
places.description: A giant kettle saluting Owensboro's barbecue and burgoo tradition.

places.name: Men made of mufflers
places.description: Folk-art figures welded together from old car mufflers.

places.name: Camp Breckinridge POW murals
places.description: Wall murals of the homeland painted by a German prisoner of war held here in World War II, preserved in the old officers' club.

places.name: World's largest fluorite collection
places.description: The Ben E. Clement Mineral Museum, packed with glowing fluorite crystals from the local mines.

places.name: Everly Brothers monument
places.description: A guitar-shaped granite monument to Don and Phil in the town they called home.

places.name: Bill Monroe's birthplace
places.description: The restored hilltop homeplace of the father of bluegrass, near his grave and a museum.

places.name: The Last Supper in concrete
places.description: A life-size concrete Last Supper sitting by the road.

places.name: Edgar Cayce and the Hopkinsville Goblins
places.description: The local museum covers both the famous psychic born nearby and the 1955 night a farm family said little silver creatures attacked their house.

places.name: King Arthur's Round Table literary park
places.description: A stone Round Table and sword in the stone on the community college campus.

places.name: Paul Bunyan muffler man
places.description: One of the classic 1960s giant fiberglass men, standing near a pink elephant and a cow in glasses.

places.name: Lightning portrait of a startled lady
places.description: Locals say lightning burned a woman's image into a window pane here. The house keeps the window on view.

places.name: Wacinton, the carved giant head
places.description: A 35-foot face carved from a single oak by Peter Toth as part of his Trail of the Whispering Giants.

places.name: Grave of Speedy the mortuary mummy
places.description: Speedy was embalmed so well in 1928 that a funeral home kept him on display for 66 years before he was finally buried.

places.name: Wooldridge Monuments
places.description: An eccentric horse trader's cemetery plot crowded with 18 statues of himself, his family, his dogs and a fox.

places.name: Lost River Cave boat tour
places.description: A boat ride into a cave that once held a nightclub in its mouth.

places.name: White squirrels of Bowling Green
places.description: A colony of white squirrels lives around the WKU campus. Spotting one is the game.

places.name: Wigwam Village No. 2
places.description: A 1937 motel of concrete teepees around a giant central one. You can still stay the night.

places.name: Dinosaur World
places.description: A walk through woods filled with more than a hundred life-size dinosaur statues.

places.name: Big Mike's Mystery House
places.description: A rock shop with a tilted mystery house and a giant mosasaur skull.

places.name: Kentucky Stonehenge
places.description: A former mayor built his own Stonehenge and other rock gardens in his yard, free to wander.

places.name: Hidden River Cave
places.description: A cave that opens right on Main Street, with the world's longest underground suspension bridge.

places.name: Cannonball stuck in a building
places.description: A Civil War cannonball lodged in a downtown wall (put back in roughly the right spot after a fire).

places.name: Giant forest trolls
places.description: Three huge wooden giants by artist Thomas Dambo hidden along the trails at Bernheim Forest.

places.name: Louisville Mega Cavern
places.description: A former limestone mine under the city with tram tours, zip lines and a holiday lights drive.

places.name: 30-foot gold statue of David
places.description: A giant gold David standing outside the 21c Museum Hotel on Main Street.

places.name: Colonel Sanders' grave
places.description: The KFC founder's grave in Cave Hill Cemetery, marked with a bust and reached by following a painted line.

places.name: Big John the grocery clerk
places.description: A giant fiberglass grocery man holding bags, left from the old Big John supermarket chain.

places.name: Big John the grocery clerk (Eldorado)
places.description: Another of the giant grocery-bag men, still standing outside a store.

places.name: Cave-in-Rock, the river pirates' cave
places.description: A wide cave in the Ohio River bluff that sheltered outlaws and river pirates around 1800. You can walk right in.

places.name: Garden of the Gods
places.description: Sandstone towers and balanced rocks above the Shawnee forest, with a short stone path along the cliff edge.

places.name: Giant Superman statue
places.description: The official hometown of Superman has a 15-foot bronze Man of Steel on the square, with a museum next door.

places.name: Charlie Birger gallows and George Harrison's visit
places.description: The old jail museum keeps the gallows used for gangster Charlie Birger, plus mementos from the 1963 visit by Beatle George Harrison.

places.name: Castle Park (Dungeons and Dragons park)
places.description: A memorial playground full of castles, dragons and wizards built by a father for his son.

places.name: Bald Knob Cross of Peace
places.description: A 111-foot white cross on one of the highest hills in southern Illinois, with a huge view.

places.name: Big Things in a Small Town
places.description: A whole town of record-size objects: rocking chair, wind chime, mailbox, pitchfork, golf tee and more, all walkable.

places.name: Effingham's giant cross
places.description: A 198-foot steel cross at the meeting of two interstates.

places.name: Where the rivers meet
places.description: A lookout at Fort Defiance where you can watch the Ohio and Mississippi run side by side in two colors.

places.name: Popeye statues
places.description: The hometown of Popeye's creator has statues of the whole cast scattered around town.

places.name: World's largest catsup bottle
places.description: A 170-foot water tower shaped like a 1949 catsup bottle.

places.name: Bell Witch Cave
places.description: The farm at the center of Tennessee's most famous haunting, with tours of the cave and a replica cabin.

places.name: Eiffel Tower replica
places.description: A 70-foot Eiffel Tower in a city park, wearing a red beret in some seasons.

places.name: The Parthenon and Athena
places.description: A full-size copy of the Parthenon with a 42-foot gilded Athena inside.

places.name: Lane Motor Museum
places.description: A collection of the strangest cars ever made: propeller cars, microcars, amphibious cars.

places.name: World's largest cedar bucket
places.description: A cedar bucket big enough to hold over 1,500 gallons, at Cannonsburgh Village.

places.name: Loretta Lynn's ranch
places.description: The singer's whole town-sized ranch, with her plantation house, a replica of her childhood cabin and a museum.
